summary:
ASTRONEX – Smart Astronaut Health Monitoring Platform

ASTRONEX is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring platform developed to support human safety during space missions. It features a centralized dashboard that monitors health indicators such as heart rate, breathing rate, oxygen levels, and cabin environmental conditions. Using AI-based anomaly detection and risk assessment, the platform identifies unusual patterns, generates emergency alerts, and provides understandable risk explanations to support Mission Control decisions.
ASTRONEX addresses the challenges of astronaut health monitoring, delayed space communication, and emergency response through health history graphs, environmental monitoring, emergency workflows, offline data synchronization, and Earth–Moon–Mars communication simulations. It also includes daily health missions, astronaut wellness activities, and interactive space games.
The current software prototype demonstrates its monitoring and alert features using simulated data, with real-time sensor integration planned for future development.
ASTRONEX is important because astronauts operate in demanding environments where early identification of potential health risks and timely responses are essential. Our goal is to contribute to safer, smarter, and more reliable future human space exploration.
details: ASTRONEX – SMART ASTRONAUT HEALTH MONITORING PLATFORM Team Name: NOVA-X Project Theme: Humans in Space – Beyond Earth, Beyond Limits 1. PROJECT OVERVIEW ASTRONEX is an AI-based Smart Astronaut Health Monitoring Platform designed to monitor astronauts' health conditions and cabin environmental factors during space missions. It provides a centralized dashboard displaying important health indicators such as heart rate, breathing rate, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), ECG, and cabin temperature. The system aims to identify unusual changes in health conditions and environmental parameters at an early stage. It provides alerts, risk assessments, and explanations to help astronauts and Mission Control teams make timely decisions. The current prototype demonstrates its functionality using simulated data. 2. WORKING PRINCIPLE ASTRONEX follows a four-stage process: 1. Input Data: Collects astronaut health indicators and cabin environmental data through simulated readings and a planned sensor integration system. 2. Data Processing: Validates collected data, compares readings with astronaut baseline values, and identifies changes and trends. 3. Riskcast AI: Uses AI-based anomaly detection and risk assessment concepts to identify unusual patterns, explain potential risks, and provide model confidence scores. 4. Mission Control: Displays health dashboards, alerts, risk explanations, monitoring graphs, and suggested areas for review. 3. KEY FEATURES AND BENEFITS - Continuous astronaut health monitoring. - Heart rate, breathing rate, SpO₂, and ECG monitoring concepts. - Cabin environmental monitoring, including CO₂, O₂, pressure, temperature, and radiation. - AI-based anomaly detection and risk assessment. - Health history graphs and trend analysis. - Emergency alerts and response workflows. - Daily health missions and astronaut wellness activities. - Interactive space games for entertainment. - Mission Control dashboard with alerts and risk explanations. - Supports early identification of unusual changes and faster decision-making. 4. OBJECTIVES AND FUTURE SCOPE Our main objective is to develop a smart and reliable health monitoring platform that supports astronaut safety during space exploration. ASTRONEX aims to identify potential health risks, provide understandable warnings, and support timely responses. Future developments include physical sensor integration, real-time health monitoring, improved AI prediction capabilities, advanced risk assessment, and enhanced communication between astronauts and Mission Control. 5. SENSOR INTEGRATION Live Data Mode: The system accepts live sensor data through a backend endpoint, POST "/api/readings". Each data submission contains the astronaut ID, sensor ID, measured value, and timestamp. Until actual hardware sends data, readings are displayed as "UNAVAILABLE" rather than displaying fake live values. Planned Hardware: - ESP32 – Microcontroller for sensor connectivity. - MAX30102 – Pulse and oxygen saturation monitoring. - AD8232 – ECG monitoring. - mmWave Radar – Contactless movement monitoring. These hardware components are planned and are not physically connected yet. Camera Monitoring: Contactless movement estimation uses the browser camera with user consent. Movement is estimated locally through frame differences, and video is not transmitted outside the device. Simulation Mode: Currently, health indicators and cabin readings such as CO₂, O₂, pressure, and radiation are simulated. Demonstration scenarios include unusual vital readings, sensor disconnection, missing data, and rising CO₂ levels. 6. SYSTEMS INTEGRATION Space–Earth Communication: The prototype demonstrates telemetry communication between spacecraft and Earth based on line-of-sight availability. During communication outages, collected data is queued and synchronized when communication becomes available again. Communication Delay Simulation: The platform demonstrates communication delays for Earth, Moon, and Mars missions. Emergency Workflow: An emergency is automatically initiated when a critical AI risk flag occurs or CO₂ exceeds twice its configured threshold. The workflow runs an emergency checklist, records an event timeline, and sends an acknowledgement to Mission Control. NASA Data Hub: Provides links to NASA resources, including: - DONKI – Space weather information. - APOD – Astronomy Picture of the Day. - CNEOS – Center for Near Earth Object Studies. - NASA Eyes – Interactive space exploration. 7. TECHNOLOGIES AND TOOLS USED Programming Languages: - HTML – Webpage structure. - CSS – Styling and user interface design. - Vanilla JavaScript – Application logic and functionality. Development Technologies: - Three.js r128 – 3D cabin and Earth globe visualization. - Canvas and SVG – Charts, graphs, and digital twin visualization. - Web Crypto – Login and cryptographic functionality. - localStorage – Local data storage. - Web Audio – Audio notifications and alerts. Additional Resources: - NASA Open Datasets and NASA APIs. - Artificial Intelligence concepts for anomaly detection and risk assessment. - Data Analytics for processing and interpreting readings. - SI (Super Intelligence) Tools for code development assistance, text preparation, and image generation. - Simulated data for prototype demonstrations. The current application is a software-based prototype developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in a single file. 8. TEAM CONTRIBUTIONS Our team collaboratively developed ASTRONEX, a smart astronaut health monitoring platform. We contributed ideas for health monitoring, health history graphs, emergency alerts, daily health missions, interactive space games, and astronaut wellness activities. Our contributions included project planning, concept development, website design, feature development, testing, and presentation preparation. Every team member contributed to creating an engaging and innovative space-health solution. 9. ASTRONAUT PROFILES The application displays four fictional astronaut profiles: - Mira Okafor - Ravi Menon - Sana Kobayashi - Leo Park These names represent fictional astronauts created for demonstrating the application's monitoring features. They are not actual team members. 10. EXPECTED OUTCOME ASTRONEX demonstrates how artificial intelligence, data analytics, sensor technology, and space communication concepts can work together in an integrated astronaut health monitoring platform. It aims to support early risk identification, emergency awareness, astronaut wellness, and improved Mission Control decision-making. CONCLUSION ASTRONEX represents our vision of combining Artificial Intelligence, health monitoring, data analytics, and space technology to support astronaut safety during future space exploration. By identifying unusual changes, explaining potential risks, and supporting timely responses, the platform aims to contribute towards safer and more reliable human space missions. ASTRONEX – SAFER MISSIONS. FASTER HELP.
